item.description:
### Added - **OpenCode is now fully integrated with Perch.** Local OpenCode sessions appear live on the Mac, iPhone, Apple Watch, widgets and Live Activities, with model, exact cost, five-part token usage, todos, subagents, notifications and Stats. Perch installs a small owned OpenCode plugin and keeps all state handling, validation and persistence in its signed Swift helper. - **OpenCode permissions and simple questions can be answered from the Mac.** Allow maps to OpenCode's one-time approval and Deny rejects it. Exactly one free-text question can be answered directly from the notification without Accessibility access; structured questions stay in OpenCode. - **OpenCode Go usage estimates.** When local sessions use `opencode-go`, Perch shows clearly labelled rolling five-hour, ISO-week and anchored-month estimates. The calculation is entirely local: no cookies, credentials or usage API calls.
### Security - OpenCode message bodies, text deltas, reasoning and attachments never cross the plugin boundary. Plugin files are owner-only and hash-verified, SQLite is opened read-only, PID reuse is checked with process start time, and older companions receive compatibility-stripped records.
### Note - **Restart any OpenCode session that's already open.** OpenCode loads plugins when it starts, so a session running while Perch updates won't report until you start a new one — it'll sit at "Idle" until then. New sessions work straight away, with nothing to set up. The same applies to Devin sessions open when you updated to 0.5.20. - Update the iPhone and watch apps alongside this version. An older companion doesn't know about OpenCode yet and will label OpenCode sessions as another agent; everything else keeps working and the label corrects itself once the phone app updates.
